sections.overview: The roundscale spearfish is a poorly documented oceanic billfish of the Atlantic and Mediterranean.
sections.identification: It resembles other spearfishes, but its rounded, multi-pointed mid-body scales and anal-fin proportions aid identification.
sections.habitat: It is pelagic and oceanic; confirmed records include Madeira, Sicily, the Strait of Gibraltar and waters off southern Portugal.
sections.diet: Species-specific dietary information is scarce in the accounts consulted.
sections.behavior: It is highly migratory, but the scale of its movements remains uncertain because records are sparse.
sections.reproduction: A 2025 study genetically confirmed an egg and a juvenile, but much of its reproductive biology remains unknown.
sections.ecology: It is occasionally encountered in fisheries, and accurate identification matters because it can be confused with other billfishes.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment listed the species as Data Deficient in 2021.
